newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker RGI fish unit fails in Chile bid.
newsitem.headline: Aker RGI fish unit fails in Chile bid.

text.p: Norway Seafoods, a unit of Norwegian holding company Aker RGI, said on Tuesday the crown court in Chile had rejected its request for a licence to fish for blue whiting in Chile's 200-mile fishing zone.
Norway Seafoods, the world's largest catcher and processor of white fish, is the owner of the American Monarch fishing vessel, the world's most expensive such vessel ever to be built.

The 400 million crown American Monarch was especially built to fish in Chilean waters and has been moored in Seattle, Washington in the United States, awaiting a decision from Chilean authorities since it was completed in 1996.
It is owned by Peaquera Yelcho S.A., the Chilean daughter company of Norway Seafoods. Norway Seafoods booked a loss on the vessel of 14 million crowns in the first quarter.
Peaquera Yelcho had applied to authorities to switch three of its permits to fish for austral, a local cod fish, into one licence for blue whiting.
Its original application was turned down on technicalities. The Chilean crown court sent the latest decision to Oslo-based Norway Seafoods late on Monday, company spokesman Frank Reite said.

"We are obviously disappointed because we believe we have not made any mistakes," Reite told Reuters. "We need a few days to study the ruling but then we will probably make an appeal to the Supreme Court."
